links.outcome: Fellow accuracy, completeness, and time-to-answer with versus without LLM assistance on vignettes
links.effect: Median accuracy rose from 72% to 85.5% (Δ +13.0%, p<0.001); completeness 1.9 to 2.5 (p<0.001); time-to-answer 7.1 to 5.9 min (p=0.002).
links.quote: Median accuracy increased from 72% (65·5-78·5) in the unaided arm to 85·5% (79·0-91·0) in the aided arm with Δ =  + 13·0%, p-value < 0·001.

links.outcome: Clinically significant hallucination and niche dose-duration knowledge gaps in LLM-aided responses
links.effect: Only a single clinically significant hallucination (3.3%) occurred; minimal or no benefit in dual infection scenarios and niche dose-duration knowledge.
links.quote: Only a single clinically significant hallucination (3·3%) occurred.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the effect of providing LLM assistance versus unassisted performance to nephrology fellows answering simulated clinical case vignettes.
